A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. The main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and matchable despite the method renaming and extensive reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original continual-adaptation experiments on Kinetics50 and VGGSound corruption benchmarks, including baseline comparisons, forgetting measurements, and ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds numerical observations tracing which earlier corruption domains supply retrieved parameters.

M1.justification: AV-CTTA is renamed AVReCAP. Fusion-layer adaptation, Gaussian/KL retrieval, EMA updates, buffer merging, and the READ losses remain unchanged, including Algorithm 1. The added explanations do not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Kinetics50 and VGGSound benchmarks with visual, audio, and bimodal corruptions. The new retrieval diagnostic uses existing Kinetics50-C coverage without introducing a new task or environment.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparators remain SOURCE, TENT, EATA, SAR, READ, SuMi, PTA, and BriMPR*. The newly discussed source-dependent method in reference [53] is explicitly excluded from evaluation.

E3.justification: v2 Section 10 adds a limited diagnostic procedure counting retrievals by originating corruption over 78 batches per task on early Kinetics50-C tasks. Existing benchmark splits, severity, batch size, optimization settings, and task-order protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The added Section 10 analysis examines whether retrieved parameters originate from related corruption domains, directly probing the retrieval mechanism. Existing forgetting, buffer, threshold, distance, batch-size, and task-order analyses are retained; the task-order study was already in v1 Appendix C.4.

E5.justification: There is no change to seed information, repeated-run reporting, uncertainty estimates, or significance testing. Both versions report point accuracies; the added retrieval counts are diagnostic outcomes rather than uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark results are retained, including Figure 5 means of 50.29% on Kinetics50-2C and 43.51% on VGGSound-2C. v2 adds retrieval counts: for example, Shot Noise retrieves Gaussian parameters in 4/78 batches and Impulse Noise in 77/78 batches.

T1.justification: The formal assumptions, update equations, and Gaussian KL derivation are unchanged. v1 Appendix A.1 becomes v2 Supplementary Section 7.1; splitting and renumbering equations does not introduce new mathematics.

C1.justification: The central claims remain source-free audio-visual continual adaptation through transferable fusion parameters, improved corruption performance, and reduced forgetting. v2 emphasizes source-free operation more explicitly, but this scope was already stated in v1.

C2.justification: v2 Section 10 explicitly links similar input statistics to similar fusion parameters and interprets the new retrieval counts as evidence of selection from related domains. The existing limitations concerning retrieval latency, architectural assumptions, and threshold tuning remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project-page URL on the title page, providing a new resource-access pointer. The PDFs do not establish what that page contains. Existing implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware information, and baseline repository links are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Zhang et al.'s Analytic Continual Test-Time Adaptation for Multi-Modality Corruption as reference [53], describes its source-data requirement, and explains its exclusion from comparisons. This modestly sharpens the paper's source-free positioning.

P1.justification: The method is renamed throughout, Section 4.5 adds a short design rationale, and Section 4.2 clarifies buffer indexing. Appendices A-D become Supplementary Sections 7-10, with limited wording, citation-style, and author-information edits. Most prose and the narrative order remain intact.

P2.justification: The document is comprehensively reformatted into a narrower single-column layout. Figures and tables are resized and relocated, headers and captions change style, and green shading replaces gray highlighting in result tables. Wide tables become substantially smaller; their numerical content is retained.

improvement.justification: The added retrieval counts provide limited direct support for the selection mechanism, while clearer explanations and the newly acknowledged source-dependent prior work improve transparency. These are modest gains: benchmark evidence is unchanged, the diagnostic does not establish parameter optimality, and the smaller tables reduce readability.
